saab_f35_wdns: Denmark picked the Saab Draken in 1968 to replace its ageing F-100s, buying 51 airframes split between strike, reconnaissance and trainer versions, none of them fitted with radar. During the 1980s the F-35 gained a laser rangefinder, ballistic computer, new HUD and RWR, and it flew until the F-16 took over in 1993. In the game it is the most ground-attack-minded Draken, with a broad selection of bombs and rockets backed by that computer, plus a pair of AIM-9Ns to protect itself. Handling is still good, but energy drains away quickly and there is no radar to fall back on. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
saab_j21a_1: Saab's twin-boom J21 was conceived around the start of the Second World War so that Sweden would not have to rely on foreign fighters; the layout was chosen for its visibility and ease of maintenance, and the engine was a modified Daimler-Benz DB 605. Over 300 were built, though none saw wartime action. In the game it is heavy and unremarkable in speed (around 640 km/h) and agility, but it absorbs a lot of damage, and its real asset is the nose battery of one 20 mm cannon and four 13.2 mm guns, which shreds most opponents. It came with the first Swedish aircraft tree in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_j21a_2: The second J21 production batch changed very little from the A-1: a divided centre flap and new cooling fins for the oil and coolant radiators, on an airframe that was already dated when it appeared. In the game it shares the A-1's flight model, so the same sturdy, firepower-first approach applies. The only meaningful difference is the cannon, with a Bofors 20 mm Akan m/45 replacing the earlier m/41A alongside the four heavy machine guns. It was added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_j21ra: Sweden's first jet was made by adapting the existing J21 airframe to take a jet engine; it first flew on 10 March 1947 and served from 1949 to 1957, proving more useful as an attacker than a fighter before the J29 and A28B replaced it. In the game it is the nation's introduction to jets: faster than the piston J21, well suited to hit-and-run attacks yet able to turn when needed. A cannon and four heavy machine guns with deep ammunition stores make it forgiving, but the wings tear off at high speed, which its airbrakes help to prevent. Added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_j29a: Saab's late-1940s J29A combined swept wings, informed by captured German research, with a licence-built de Havilland Ghost engine; it first flew in 1948, served with the Flygvapnet from 1951 to 1962 and never fought. In the game it accelerates slowly and loses speed in turns that it struggles to regain, so it suits hit-and-run passes and teamwork rather than drawn-out dogfights, even though it turns respectably while fast. Four 20 mm Akan m/47C cannons, licensed Hispano Mk V copies with a slower rate of fire, and plenty of ammunition give it more punch than the J21RA. Introduced in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_j29b: The A29B was a J29 pressed into the attack role while Sweden waited for a purpose-built strike aircraft, and it gained deflatable internal fuel tanks that gave it more fuel options than the J29A. It keeps the J29A's guns and adds powerful rockets, though with no ballistic computer to aim them. Clean of ordnance it flies like the fighter it is, so in ground battles a sensible pattern is to spend the rockets on easy targets early and then turn to hunting enemy aircraft. It joined the game in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_j29d: The J29D was Sweden's try at a quick-climbing interceptor for hunting bombers, built on the swept-wing Tunnan, and although it never went supersonic it could exceed 1,060 km/h at some altitudes. Its stubby looks hide a hard-hitting jet: four 30 mm cannons in the nose and a choice of attack rockets let it fly interception, air superiority or fast strike sorties depending on loadout, and it can charge in, do damage and leave before opponents react. It came as a premium pack in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack", left the store after the 9th Anniversary Sale and briefly returned for Golden Eagles during the 2023 "Swedish Air Force Day" event.
saab_j29f: Last of the J29 Tunnan line, the J29F served from 1955 to 1976 before the J32B replaced it, and it was the only version cleared to carry RB24 air-to-air missiles. It also received the RM 2B engine with afterburner, giving it more speed and much better energy recovery than the J29A. In the game it is a balanced fighter that turns well at high speed, yet it remains slow beside many opposing jets, so it does best supporting teammates or diving on distracted targets; the RB24s are handy for forcing an opponent to turn into gun range. Added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_j32b: An all-weather fighter and interceptor, the J32B entered Swedish service in 1958; 118 were built, 26 of which were involved in accidents, and the J35 replaced it in the 1970s. Over the A32A it gained the stronger RM6A engine, four 30 mm Akan m/55 cannons and air-to-air missile capability. In the game its strong climb rate lets it get above opponents, dive in with heavy firepower and use the built-up speed to escape and climb again. The afterburner is a useful way out of trouble, though it burns through fuel quickly. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_j35a: Designed to replace both the J29 and the J32B, the J35 Draken became the first fully supersonic aircraft fielded in Western Europe. Ninety J35As were built in short-tailed A1 and long-tailed A2 forms, the latter's bigger afterburner requiring a retractable tail wheel, and the first 1960 batch lacked radar and gunsights. In the game it is capable but carries no countermeasures, so keeping speed up to outrun missiles and watching the sky closely matter a great deal. Its four RB24 (AIM-9B) missiles are basic but work when dropped on unaware targets from altitude. Added in Update "Direct Hit", it left sale after the 2023 May Sale and returns only occasionally.
saab_j35d: The fourth Draken version, the J35D received an uprated RM 6C engine, and 120 were delivered to the Swedish Air Force in 1963 and 1964. In the game it is quick and agile: the first Swedish jet able to reach Mach 2 and the first aircraft in War Thunder able to perform the Cobra manoeuvre. The delta wing makes it shed speed heavily when manoeuvring, though, and its ammunition supply is small. It was added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
saab_j35j: The J35J traces back to the J35F, which brought a Mod.67 afterburner, AIM-4 and AIM-26 missiles, a Hughes IRST and an S7B fire control system at the cost of one 30 mm cannon; from 1985 Sweden upgraded its Drakens to J35J standard with a datalink, more cannon ammunition and two extra missile hardpoints, and flew them until 1999. In the game it is essentially a J35XS without countermeasures: fast and highly manoeuvrable, but it bleeds energy quickly in turns and the cannon is unimpressive. Introduced in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
saab_j35xs: Finland asked Sweden for a Draken close to the J35J standard, and the result was the J35XS: 12 were produced from Saab kits and assembled in Finland, with better electronics and countermeasures, more pylons and RB24J (AIM-9P) missiles. In the game it flies like other Drakens, fast with good high-AoA ability but losing speed in hard manoeuvres, while the double delta holds energy well at high speed at some cost to agility. Its six RB24Js work best against unaware targets, and 12 countermeasures are thin cover, so flying low to stay out of radar locks pays off. The IRST locks jets silently but cannot tell friend from foe. Added in Update "Apex Predators".
saab_ja37: The JA37C was a 1980s upgrade that kept the Viggen relevant while the Gripen was still years away, adding a new signal processor, countermeasures and the PS-46/A radar, able to track several targets at once; all were later converted to JA37D standard. In the game it is a generalist rather than a standout, with neither the best flight performance nor the biggest weapon load, but its all-aspect pulse-Doppler radar is unusually advanced for its rank, and it can turn with heavier jets such as the F-4 Phantom while firing RB-24J and RB71 Skyflash missiles. Introduced in Update "Direct Hit".
saab_ja37d: The JA37D brought the JA37C up to date with new avionics, navigation systems, a modernised cockpit and pod-mounted electronic countermeasures, while keeping the PS 46/A radar and gaining RB 99 (AIM-120 AMRAAM) capability so it could serve until the Gripen arrived. In the game it handles much like its predecessor, with weak acceleration and a modest top speed but a tight turn from the delta wing. The key addition is the RB 74 (AIM-9L), a capable short-to-medium range infrared missile that lets it fight from altitude against targets below, though enemy radar missiles remain a threat. Added in Update "Apex Predators".
saab_ja37di: After the Cold War Sweden moved towards closer NATO cooperation, and in the early 2000s 21 JA37Ds were reworked for interoperability (the "I"), chiefly by fitting the FR31 radio; they retired with the other Viggen fighters in 2004. In the game the change that matters is the RB 99, Sweden's AIM-120. The missiles are effective, but they cannot hide the airframe's age: it lacks the speed and agility of its opponents, and both radar and RWR are dated, which makes it hard work to fly well. It was added in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
saab_ja37di_f21: This JA37DI carries the markings of F21 at Luleå, a wing formed in 1941 to defend Norrbotten that progressed from Beechcraft transports to Vampires, J32Bs and, from 1983, Viggens, before converting to the JAS39 in 2004; it still flies Gripens today. The DI standard itself was a NATO-interoperability upgrade of 21 JA37Ds, centred on a new FR31 radio. In battle it is identical to the regular JA37DI apart from the camouflage: RB 99 (AIM-120) missiles are a real asset, but the jet is slow and unwieldy for its rank and its radar and RWR are outdated. Introduced in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
saab_jas39a: Saab's JAS39A Gripen entered Swedish service in 1996, replacing the JA37D and AJS37 as a multirole jet for air defence, strike and reconnaissance. Added in Update "Air Superiority" as Sweden's top-rank fighter, it is a much fairer match for MiG-29s and F-16s than the JA37D was. Air-to-air missiles cover the fighter role, while several bomb loadouts make it useful in support of ground forces. Its handling departs from the Viggen's and will feel closer to an F-16 for pilots who know that jet.
saab_jas39c: The JAS39C was Saab's pitch to former Warsaw Pact states that wanted NATO-compatible fighters but could not afford top American jets: a Gripen brought up to late F-16C standard, with greater NATO interoperability, more ordnance options and aerial refuelling. It first flew on 6 September 2002 and, while it sold far less widely than the F-16, it did replace old MiGs in Hungary and the Czech Republic. In the game it improves on the JAS39A with a glass cockpit and, crucially, the RB 99 (AIM-120A AMRAAM), BOL dispensers with more than 700 countermeasures, and helmet-cued radar targeting, on a small, light, agile airframe. It arrived in Update "Seek & Destroy".
saab_jas39c_hungary: Hungary joined NATO in 1999 and in 2003 chose to lease 14 Gripens from Sweden rather than buy F-16s or upgrade its MiG-29s; delivered by 2007 as JAS 39A/Bs, they were later raised to C/D standard with a PS-05/Mk.4 radar, an extension kept the lease running to 2026 and four more were ordered in 2024. In the Italian tree it differs from other Gripens by carrying AGM-65G and AGM-65H Mavericks. It is small and agile, with BOL pylons holding up to 732 flares, AIM-9s and AIM-120s for air combat and JDAMs or laser-guided bombs for ground work, though total payload is limited. Added in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
saab_jas39c_south_africa: South Africa became the Gripen's first export customer in 1999, ordering 26 (17 C and 9 D models) to replace its Mirage III-derived Cheetahs; deliveries ran from 2008 to 2012 and the jets guarded the 2010 World Cup, though funding shortfalls and maintenance troubles grounded the fleet in 2021. The British tree's first South African jet, it pairs strong thrust-to-weight, acceleration, climb, agility and energy retention with guided bombs, AGM-65 Mavericks, R-Darter active radar missiles and AIM-9Ms. It is at its best in a dogfight, so heavy loads blunt it, and its radar holds locks well but is imprecise. Added in Update "Air Superiority".
saab_jas39c_thailand: Thailand ordered twelve Gripens in two batches of six, in 2008 and 2010, to replace its F-5s; all had arrived by September 2013 and the type became the core of the national air defence network. It came with the Thai aviation line in the Japanese tree in Update "Storm Warning" and is one of the most balanced aircraft at its rank, pairing good flight performance with a modern self-protection suite and BOL pods. AIM-9M and AIM-120 missiles, though few in number, let it compete at short and long range, while four AGM-65s and a thermal targeting pod with good zoom make it one of Japan's strongest close air support options.
saab_jas39d: The JAS39D is the two-seat Gripen, developed alongside the modernised C model chiefly for training but able to fly the same air defence, strike and reconnaissance missions; the second cockpit costs it some internal fuel and its cannon. In the game it keeps the C's strengths: excellent handling, a wide range of external stores, and AIM-9M and Rb 99 (AIM-120) missiles for air combat. The missing 27 mm gun and a limited number of air-to-air missiles are its main drawbacks. It was introduced in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
saab_jas39e: The Gripen E is a larger, heavier evolution of the Gripen C, with an ES-05 AESA radar, IRST, a stronger General Electric F414 engine, a wide cockpit display, two more hardpoints and roughly 2,000 kg of extra payload. Sweden ordered 60 in 2013 and took the first in October 2025; Brazil flies it as the F-39E. In the game it can carry seven RB 99s plus two RB 74(M)s, and the AESA set finds and tracks targets more reliably than the C's mechanical PS-05, and the F414 offsets the extra weight. For ground attack it takes up to 16 SPICE 250 glide bombs and Brimstone missiles. Added in Update "Line of Contact".
saab_sk60b: The Saab 105 started in 1959 as a twin-jet project for civil and military customers that ended up purely military; the prototype flew in 1963, Sweden ordered 150 in 1964, 60 were later adapted for ground attack, and Austria bought 40. In the game the SK60B is a very light, nimble trainer turned attacker, but its engines are weak and it is outperformed by the Su-11 and even by the Vampire. It cannot carry bombs, relying instead on rockets and RB05 MACLOS guided missiles, and its guns compete with those missiles for the same pylons. It arrived in Update "New Power".
saab_t18b_1: Saab's T18B began as a torpedo-bomber version of the twin-engined Saab 18, but it proved too fast for the low, slow drops torpedoes required, so it was reworked into an attacker armed with a pair of 20 mm akan m/41 cannons under the nose, keeping its enlarged bomb bay; it served from 1947 until 1956–57. In the game it reaches about 595 km/h, and its forward cannons hit hard enough to be useful against ground targets as well as aircraft. Rear defence is thin, with only one machine gun, while ordnance options include rockets, bombs and torpedoes. Added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
saab_t18b_2: This T18B is the heavy-gun version of Saab's Swedish attack bomber, mounting a 57 mm akan m/47 autocannon fed from a 41-round magazine to deal with armoured ground targets. Between its flight performance and that cannon it behaves more like a disguised attacker than a bomber, although carrying such a large gun brings drawbacks of its own. It was added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
sagittario_2: Aerfer's Sagittario 2 was an Italian Cold War prototype entered in the contest for a standard NATO light fighter, which the Fiat G.91 won; Aerfer went on to develop it into the Ariete, which added a second engine. In the game it is one of Italy's most agile, dogfight-friendly jets, handling well and carrying two fast-firing cannons that wreck most aircraft they hit. Its small fuel load limits time in the air, so overextending is risky. It was introduced in Update "Red Skies".
sb2c_1c: Curtiss's SB2C Helldiver, ordered as the Dauntless's successor, first flew in December 1940, but poor handling, stability and structural problems held up production until 1943 and brought a damaging Truman Committee report; even so it became the US Navy's main late-war dive bomber, with 7,140 built. The SB2C-1C, the first variant to see combat, swapped four machine guns for two 20 mm cannons and gained hydraulic flaps. In the game it can carry a torpedo or naval mine, and its cannons plus an air spawn let it act as a makeshift interceptor, but it flies poorly and its two rear guns offer little defence. Added in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
sb2c_4: Built in greater numbers than any other Helldiver, with 2,045 completed from late 1944 until the SB2C-5 took over in 1945, the SB2C-4 paired an uprated R-2600-20 Cyclone with new wing racks. In the game it is a straightforward improvement on the SB2C-1C, accelerating better and offering more varied loadouts: the racks take an extra pair of bombs, HVAR rockets or gun pods for strafing soft targets or attacking aircraft. It is still sluggish on the controls, and its weak rear guns do little to discourage pursuers. Added in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
sb2c_5_france: France bought 110 SB2C-5 Helldivers in 1949 to replace its Dauntlesses and flew them from carriers until 1958; their only combat was in Indochina. The Helldiver was a large Curtiss dive bomber with an R-2600 Twin Cyclone and an internal bomb bay, though poor survivability meant the Hellcat often did the same job better. In the game it is all but identical to the American SB2C-1C and SB2C-4, minus the 1,000 lb Type A magnetic mine. Besides dive bombing, its solid guns and bomber spawn let it hunt aircraft, and once rid of its payload it turns surprisingly well. Added in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
sb2c_5_greece: In the final phase of the Greek Civil War the United States supplied 48 SB2C-5 Helldivers, shipped aboard the escort carrier USS Sicily in spring 1949 and handed to the Royal Hellenic Air Force's 336th Bomber Squadron; they saw short but heavy fighting and were retired in 1953, and one is displayed at the Hellenic Air Force Museum. In the Israeli tree it matches the French SB2C-5 exactly. Dive bombing and attack are its main jobs, but decent guns and a bomber spawn make it a capable aircraft hunter too, and with its load gone it can out-turn unwary fighters. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
sb2c_5_thailand: Twelve surplus SB2C-5 Helldivers went to Thailand after the war, shared between the navy and air force and used against the communist insurgency in the north during the 1950s; one survives in the air force museum in Bangkok. In the Japanese tree it fills a slot similar to the B7A2 Ryusei but behaves more like a classic dive bomber: sluggish, particularly when loaded, yet able to lift twice the Ryusei's ordnance, including a 2,000 lb bomb. Gun pods with four .50 cal Brownings plus an air spawn also let it chase bombers. It was a reward from Battle Pass Season XVIII, "The Last Legionaire", in Update "Storm Warning".
sb2u-2: The SB2U carrier dive bomber dated from the early 1930s and was considered obsolete by 1939, yet it stayed in front-line use through Midway before moving to training units in 1943. Its constant-speed propeller doubled as a dive brake, and it could carry a 250 lb bomb under each wing plus a 500 or 1,000 lb centreline bomb on a trapeze that swung it clear of the propeller. In the game it is slow but sturdy and a capable dive bomber, lowering its landing flaps to control speed in place of dive brakes. Wing guns handle soft targets and a 7.7 mm rear gun copes with biplanes. Added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
sb2u-3: Already dated by 1939, the SB2U dive bomber still served through Midway before retiring to training duties in 1943, carrying two 250 lb wing bombs and a 500 or 1,000 lb centreline bomb on a swinging trapeze. The SB2U-3 has a slightly weaker Pratt & Whitney R-1535-2 than the SB2U-2 and is marginally slower, but the same bomb load remains effective against armoured ships and ground targets. Its big gain is four 12.7 mm Brownings in place of two 7.7 mm guns, so despite mediocre handling it can take on biplanes and early monoplanes, especially with incendiary belts. Introduced in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
sb_25j_netherlands: In 1941 the exiled Dutch government placed an order for 162 B-25Cs to defend the East Indies and received 150, among them SB-25s with extra nose guns, followed by B-25Js from 1944. After the war the 18th Bomber Squadron flew Mitchells, usually without the top turret and with more nose guns, against the Indonesian revolution until 1949; the last Dutch Mitchell unit disbanded in July 1950. In the French tree it is a close relative of the B-25J, versatile thanks to a good payload, strong guns and solid survivability, but the extra forward firepower does nothing for its poor handling. It was a reward from Battle Pass Season XX, "Flying Dragon".
sb_2m_100: Tupolev's SB answered a 1933 Soviet call for a fast twin-engined bomber; the Hispano-Suiza-powered ANT-40 IS prototype flew on 30 December 1934, and after various problems production began in late 1935 with licence-built Klimov M-100 engines. The SB 2M-100A soon followed with uprated M-100A engines, and several hundred were built. In the game it is fast and its defensive guns are good enough to see off biplanes, but it has next to no armour, a light bomb load for its class and a very poor climb rate. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
sb_2m_103_mv3: Combat over Spain and China showed that SB bombers were easy prey for fighters attacking from behind, so the SB 2M-103 was given a spherical MV-3 rear turret with a far wider field of fire; trials began in 1937, but few aircraft carried it before 1940. In the game it is a dedicated bomber: slow to climb and clumsy in turns, yet faster than most pre-war designs, with three ShKAS turrets that cover it well. It has been available since the open beta test that preceded Update 1.27.
sb_2m_103c: Also known as the SBbis, the SB 2M-103 updated Tupolev's most-produced design, the SB-2 (ANT-40), with 960 hp M-103 engines, a reworked navigator's position, a steerable tail wheel and optional retractable skis. It was tested from September 1937 to September 1938, and an early example carried a one-tonne load to record altitudes of 12,244 m and then 12,692 m. In the game it is best kept to bombing runs, as it climbs and turns poorly, but it outpaces pre-war aircraft and three ShKAS turrets defend it dependably. It has been in the game since the open beta, ahead of Update 1.27.
sb_2m_103u: Built in the second half of 1939, the SB 2M-103U version of Tupolev's SB-2 (ANT-40) introduced liquid cooling for its M-103A engines through adjustable air ducts. SB 2M bombers fought in Spain, China, Finland and the opening phase of the German-Soviet war. In the game its job is bombing: climb and manoeuvrability are weak, but it can outrun pre-war types, and its three ShKAS turrets give reliable protection. It has been present since the open beta test before Update 1.27.
sb_2m_103u_china: From autumn 1937 the Soviet Union sent several dozen SB bombers of various versions to help Kuomintang China against Japan, and this SB 2M-103U, with regulated air ducts cooling its M-103A engines, wears Chinese Nationalist colours. It plays just like the Soviet example: a bomber above all, slow to climb and unwieldy, but quicker than pre-war aircraft and well guarded by three ShKAS turrets. It joined the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
sb_2m_103u_mv3: This SB 2M-103U variant paired tunnel radiators for its M-103A engines, which reshaped the nacelles and cut drag, with an MV-3 spherical upper turret that let the gunner fire across nearly the whole upper hemisphere. In the game it is used mainly for bombing; it climbs slowly and is far from agile, but it is faster than pre-war aircraft and its three ShKAS turrets deter attackers reliably. It has been in the game since the start of open beta testing, before Update 1.27.
sb_2m_105: Fitted with M-105 engines that were stronger and easier to run than those of the SB 2M-103U, this upgrade of Tupolev's SB was built in a batch of about 150 before the design was developed into the Ar-2. In the game it carries a decent load for its size and is remarkably agile, able to out-turn clumsier fighters and damage them with its twin forward ShKAS guns. Its rear is thinly defended, though, with just one ShKAS each in the dorsal and ventral turrets. It has been in the game since the open beta before Update 1.27.
sbd-3: From 1940 until late 1944 the Dauntless was the US Navy's principal carrier dive bomber, ranging about 1,700 km with two 12.7 mm cowling guns and up to 2,250 lb of bombs; it sank the Shōhō at the Coral Sea and four carriers at Midway in June 1942. One of the first American bombers in the game, the SBD-3 can air spawn and drop its bombs before fighters climb to meet it. Its guns are strong for its era, gun pods let it tackle bombers such as the He 111 or Ju 88, and it can out-turn sluggish fighters like the MiG-3. It has been in the game since the open beta.
sc_1: Curtiss proposed the SC-1 Seahawk in 1942 to replace the Kingfisher and Seagull observation floatplanes; the Navy ordered 500 before the prototype flew in February 1944, and 577 were delivered, able to operate on wheels or floats. It saw little combat apart from the 1945 Borneo campaign, and helicopters had replaced it by 1949. In the game it handles decently but is fairly slow, and its two 12.7 mm M2 Brownings plus a pair of 250 lb bombs make for a useful armament. Added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
scimitar_f1: Supermarine's final production aircraft, the Scimitar was a low-level naval strike fighter with two Rolls-Royce Avon 202s, and no heavier or more powerful aircraft had served with the Fleet Air Arm when it arrived in 1958. Unreliable, and with over half of the 76 built lost in accidents, it was moved to second-line duties once the Buccaneer arrived in 1962 and retired in 1970. In the game it is among the fastest subsonic aircraft and accelerates and climbs hard, but weak rudder response at speed makes its four ADEN cannons tricky to aim; four AIM-9Bs help. It was also the first British aircraft to carry air-to-ground missiles. Added in Update "Starfighters".
scout_ah_mk1: The Scout started out as Saunders-Roe's P.531 light utility design and became a Westland product after the early-1960s takeover; it first flew in August 1960, spawned the naval Wasp, and the two types served in Borneo, the Falklands and Northern Ireland, with around 280 built. In the game it is Britain's first helicopter and a place to learn rotary-wing flying: light, quick and agile like its successors, and fitted with ATGMs from the start. It has no armour or countermeasures and only modest weaponry, so surviving enemy air defences takes practice and care. Added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
se_203: France already built Vampires under licence and chose the Sea Venom as its first naval jet, produced by SNCASE with Fiat-built engines and entering service as the Aquilon in 1953. The SE.203 added an American AN/APQ-65 radar for all-weather work and air-to-air missiles; the type gave way to the Étendard IVM and F-8E Crusader in 1967. In the game it shares the British Sea Venom's airframe, with a strong engine giving good speed and reasonable agility, though it bleeds energy. Four 20 mm cannons hit hard, and its missiles, while not very agile, can bring down large, slow targets such as bombers. Added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
sea_fury_fb11: Hawker's Sea Fury FB 11 inherits the Tempest II's Bristol Centaurus radial and slim, cannon-armed wing, adding a wide-track undercarriage that makes deck landings easier than in the Seafires. In the game it is fast, climbs well and is surprisingly nimble, with four 20 mm Hispano Mk V cannons sharing 580 rounds, plus 250 or 500 lb bombs and RP-3 rockets for fighter-bomber work. Like other Hawkers it lives on energy: opponents it cannot out-turn it can usually out-dive. As one of the last piston fighters it meets the best propeller aircraft and early jets, yet holds its own. Added in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
sea_fury_fb51: After the war the Royal Netherlands Navy rebuilt around the carrier HNLMS Karel Doorman, ordering Sea Fury F.50s in 1946 and 1948 before Fokker licence-built 25 FB.51s, the export form of the FB.11; they left carrier service in August 1955, gave way to Sea Hawks by April 1957, and one survives at the National Military Museum. In the French tree it is a powerful fighter that rolls very quickly and keeps its energy well, but it is not agile in sustained manoeuvring and struggles against jets. It was added in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
sea_harrier_fa2: Lessons from the Falklands led Britain to order an improved Sea Harrier in 1984; shorn of its reconnaissance and strike tasks it became the FA.2 fleet defence fighter, built around the compact but capable Blue Vixen radar that enabled AIM-120 AMRAAM use, and entered service in April 1993. In the game it trails the AV-8B+ in most respects, but IRCCM-equipped AIM-9Ms, AMRAAMs, that radar and BOL countermeasures let it fight above its class. The first-generation airframe flies poorly, so VIFFing is key in dogfights, and uniquely among Harriers it can swap one or both gun pods for extra missiles. Introduced in Update "Seek & Destroy".
sea_hawk_fga50_netherlands: Funded through NATO, the Dutch Navy ordered Sea Hawk Mk.50 ground-attack jets in the mid-1950s; apart from a Philips UHF radio they matched British aircraft, later gained the ability to carry two AIM-9 Sidewinders, and 22 served from 1957 to 1964. In the French tree it is a robust attacker that can still fight in the air: the straight wing and Nene engine leave it behind swept-wing MiGs, but flown clean with two AIM-9Bs it becomes competitive, provided the missiles are watched for locking onto friendlies or the sun. Its four cannons wreck fighters and bombers when aimed at vital areas. Added in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
sea_hawk_fga6: Hawker's Sea Hawk grew from a late-war plan to fit a Rolls-Royce Nene into a modified Sea Fury; officials were lukewarm, but the Navy took three prototypes for their range. Overtaken by newer types like the Scimitar and Sea Vixen, it left production in 1956 but served Germany, the Netherlands and India, fighting at Suez and in the 1965 and 1971 Indo-Pakistani wars. In the game it is a ground attacker first, with bombs, rockets and four 20 mm cannons, yet its straight wing out-turns many transonic opponents, and careful use of flaps and airbrakes can make faster jets overshoot. Added in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
sea_hawk_mk100: After Britain ended Sea Hawk production in 1956, West Germany's navy picked it for both day fighter-bomber and all-weather duties, buying 32 Mk.100s and 32 radar-podded Mk.101s. In the game the Mk.100 is above all a strong ground attacker but can fight in the air too: the straight wing and Nene engine handicap it against swept-wing MiGs, though a clean loadout with two AIM-9Bs makes it a real threat, provided the Sidewinders do not stray onto friendlies or the sun. It was a premium pack from Update 1.87 "Locked On" until the 2021 May Sale and has since returned for Golden Eagles during German Unity Day events.
sea_venom_faw20: The Royal Navy's first navalised Venom was the two-seat FAW.20, adapted from the NF.2 night fighter with folding wings, a tailhook and a stronger undercarriage; it served as a carrier interceptor from 1951 until the Sea Vixen began replacing it in 1959, with the last leaving second-line duties in 1970. In the game the extra naval weight blunts much of the land-based Venom's performance, though its powerful engine still makes it one of the quickest aircraft it meets. Turning fights drain its energy rapidly, so fast slashing passes followed by a quick exit work far better. Added in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
seafire_fr47: Where the Seafire XVII is a low-level fighter, the FR 47 is built for altitude: its second supercharger gear peaks at 8.4 km, so it does its best work above about 6–7 km and can still engage aircraft as high as 12 km. Secondary options include two 250 lb or two 500 lb bombs, the heavier pair suiting vehicles and pillboxes, or four or eight RP-3 rockets, which are inaccurate enough that the larger salvo is usually the better pick. In mixed battles bombs tend to be more useful than rockets, except against targets with exposed crews. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
seafire_mk17: By late 1944 the Seafire had progressed through the Griffon-powered Mk XV to the F Mk XVII, which added stronger wings and landing gear and an extra fuselage fuel tank; 232 were built. In the game it builds on the Seafire LF Mk III, with the Griffon bringing a clear jump in speed and general performance, and bomb racks let it switch between air-to-air and strike work. The 7.7 mm machine guns lack punch, however, and it is heavier than land-based Spitfires. Added in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
seafire_mk3: Derived from the Spitfire Vc, the Seafire Mk III was the first naval Spitfire with manually folding wings, letting carriers stow more fighters, and it gained a Merlin 55 or 55M engine; 1,220 were built, more than any other Seafire. In the game it flies much like the Spitfire Vc, with two 20 mm Hispano Mk II cannons and four 7.7 mm Brownings in the wings. Speed and climb trail rivals such as the Bf 109 G-6 and Fw 190 A-5, but superb agility and good energy retention in turns keep it competitive. Added in Update "Winged Lions".
seafire_mk3_france: After the war France took on 141 Seafire LF Mk.IIIs, which flew over Indochina mostly in close support and raids on enemy camps. Compared with a standard Spitfire it climbs, accelerates and reaches top speed poorly, and the engine readily overheats on WEP; its cannons are also prone to jams and overheating until the Mk.II 1943 cannon modification is researched. It remains a strong dogfighter that can beat P-51s and Bf 109s in comparable conditions, but weak energy retention punishes long engagements. It was introduced in Update "Winged Lions".
shackleton_mr_mk_2: The last military branch of the Lancaster family, the Shackleton was developed from the Avro Lincoln in 1945 for anti-submarine and maritime patrol work, with a ventral radar bulge, Griffon engines driving contra-rotating propellers, and 20 mm Hispano Mk.V cannons on a flexible mount in place of the tail gunner. In the game it is an odd cousin of the Lincoln B Mk II: more mobile and heavier-hitting but less well defended and less durable. Its maximum bomb load can destroy three bases, and the Griffons let it either climb steadily as a conventional long-range bomber or run fast on WEP. Added in Update "Direct Hit".
sm_79_1936: SIAI's S.M.79 Sparviero, designed under Alessandro Marchetti, began as a civil aircraft before a bomber prototype was built; it entered service in 1936, and the first 24 production machines, with a longer dorsal hump and no roof windows, arrived by early 1937. Fast enough to evade most fighters of its day, it fought for Franco in Spain and became the mainstay of Italy's bomber force, with 1,458 built. In the German tree it suits bombing bases or ground targets, with useful but blind-spotted guns; it shrugs off machine-gun fire, and its speed and dive limit let it escape some fighters. It has been in the game since the open beta.
sm_79_1936_italy: The three-engined S.M.79 serie 1 joined the Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", after an equivalent had already served in the German line-up. Its speed is high for a bomber at its rank, especially in a shallow dive, and that is its main defence. Bomb options trail the He 111 and Ju 88 and the gunners' arcs are poor, but their 12.7 mm Breda-SAFATs hit hard, and the pilot's fixed forward Breda can strafe trucks or snipe planes. It out-turns the He 111 H-3 yet bleeds energy fast, and 500 kg bombs help against pillboxes and heavier tanks while cutting the total load from 1,250 to 1,000 kg.
sm_79_1937: Built from 1937, the Serie 4 Sparviero revised the dorsal fairing and gunner's canopy, added a fixed loop radio compass antenna, and swapped the single side-firing 7.7 mm Lewis for two Breda-SAFATs. By 1943 the type was outclassed as a bomber and reassigned to torpedo work, and after Italy changed sides it fought for both camps until 1945. In the German tree it matches the Serie 8 in performance, guns and bombs, and still knocks out ground targets effectively. The trouble is the cannon-armed fighters it often meets: it can neither outrun nor withstand them, and its guns struggle to keep them away. It has been in the game since the open beta.
sm_79_1939: The 1939 Serie 8 changed little outwardly beyond moving the right engine's exhaust to the outside of the nacelle, but it gained new fuel injection that enabled engine boost, and a stiffer, reinforced wing. Reggiane, Macchi and AUSA joined SIAI in building the type from 1938, turning out 1,218 by 1944, with 240 more licence-built in Romania. In the German tree it plays like its predecessor apart from that temporary boost: a versatile ground-attack bomber that tolerates machine-gun fire but cannot absorb cannon hits, with solid defensive guns that nonetheless leave many blind spots. It has been in the game since the open beta.
sm_79_1939_italy: Externally the 1939 Serie 8 is distinguished mainly by its right engine exhaust, moved to the nacelle's outboard side; inside, revised fuel injection allowed engine boost and the wing was strengthened. SIAI, Reggiane, Macchi and AUSA built 1,218 S.M.79s between them by 1944, while Romania produced another 240 under licence. In the Italian tree it differs from the previous model only by its boost function, which briefly raises engine power. It remains well suited to destroying ground targets and copes reasonably with machine-gun fire, though cannon fire is another matter, and its decent defensive armament has plenty of gaps. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
sm_79_1941: AS stands for aerosilurante, Italian for torpedo bomber: as new Allied monoplane fighters drove up Sparviero losses from 1940, part of the fleet switched to torpedo attack and did as well there as it had in bombing. The 1941 aircraft gained flame-damped exhausts for night operations and a torpedo mount set off-centre under the fuselage. In the German tree it edges earlier versions on speed and agility and adds one 450 mm torpedo to its bombs, making it useful in naval battles too. Its problem is the opposition: faster, cannon-armed fighters it can no longer outrun, against which its guns achieve little. It has been in the game since the open beta.
sm_79_1941_italy: The S.M.79 AS (aerosilurante, or torpedo bomber) came about once Allied monoplane fighters began inflicting heavy losses on Sparvieri in 1940; converted aircraft proved as effective with torpedoes as they had been with bombs, and 1941 production added flame-damping exhausts for night work and an off-centre torpedo mount under the fuselage. In the Italian tree it edges the previous variant on speed and handling and carries one 450 mm torpedo alongside its bombs, so it contributes in air, ground and naval battles alike. At its rank, though, it meets faster opponents and cannon-armed fighters that leave its defensive guns outmatched. It was added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
sm_79_1942: As S.M.79 bomber losses mounted from 1942, production turned towards torpedo work, and the bis/N appeared by early 1943 with a 1,430-litre fuselage tank in place of some bombs, a torpedo mount and a backup compass for magnetic-fuzed torpedoes. From 1944 Sparvieri fought on both sides until the war ended. In the German tree it is effectively an S.M.79 AS, decently fast and fairly agile for a bomber and useful in air, ground and naval battles. Its guns deter novice fighter pilots, but blind spots leave it open to coordinated attacks, and one good cannon burst can bring it down. It has been in the game since the open beta.
sm_79_1943: T.M. stood for totalmente modificato: in 1943 the S.M.79s of 132 Gruppo were rebuilt in the field, losing the ventral gondola and gaining a 700-litre fuel tank in place of bombs, armour for the cockpit and gunner stations, and 12.7 mm guns instead of two 7.7 mm weapons, after heavy losses had ended pure bomber production in 1942. In the German tree the armour markedly improves crew survival at a small cost in performance, and the heavier guns add defensive punch, but losing the gondola gun leaves the lower rear exposed. It remains effective against ground and naval targets. It has been in the game since the open beta.
sm_79_1943_italy: The bis/T.M. ("totalmente modificato", fully modified) was a 1943 field conversion of 132 Gruppo's aircraft, made after Italy stopped building pure bomber variants in 1942 amid heavy losses: the ventral gondola came off, a 700-litre tank replaced the bombs, armour was fitted around the crew, and two 7.7 mm guns gave way to heavier 12.7 mm Bredas. In the Italian tree the armour makes the crew much harder to knock out, though the extra weight costs a little performance. Defensive fire is stronger overall, but without the gondola gun the lower rear is uncovered. It still hits ground and naval targets well. Added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
sm_79_iar: Romania asked for a twin-engined S.M.79 in 1936, and the S.M.79B that followed in 1939 used licence-built Gnome-Rhône K14 radials, a glazed nose without the forward-gun hump, a raised cockpit and a slightly larger tail; 24 were ordered and IAR later built 80 more with Jumo 211s. In the game it carries the trimotor's bomb load but is slower, climbs worse and has no forward guns, and only its dorsal gun has good vertical coverage. A big elevator makes it agile until the controls stiffen beyond 390 km/h. Long in the German tree, it stopped being researchable there when Update 1.69 moved it to Italy.
sm_79_iar_italy: The twin-engined S.M.79B was built for Romania, which approached the manufacturer in 1936; completed in 1939, it replaced the trimotor layout with two licence-built Gnome-Rhône K14 radials and gained a glazed nose and raised cockpit, losing the forward-gun hump. Two engines meant less speed and climb, and after 24 were ordered IAR built 80 more with German Jumo 211s. In the Italian tree it has the S.M.79's bomb load but no offensive guns and weak defensive coverage, with only the dorsal gun offering a wide vertical arc. A large elevator gives it good agility until controls stiffen above 390 km/h. Added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
sm_91: Italy's SM.91 answered a 1942 need for a fighter to counter the bombers speeding the Allied advance: a twin-engined design with DB 601 engines, six forward 20 mm MG 151s and a gunner-operated turret with another. Two prototypes flew from 11 May 1943 but were never officially evaluated; the Germans seized one and bombing destroyed the other. In the game it resembles a typical heavy fighter, and one burst from the nose cannons can wreck aircraft and even light or medium tanks, yet it recovers lost speed more readily than most of its class. The 20 mm rear turret is a genuine deterrent to pursuers. Added in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
sm_92: Developed from the SM.88, the SM.92 was a twin-engined Italian fighter-bomber prototype powered by two DB 605s; completed in 1943 but not flown in tests until 1944, it disappointed, was damaged when a C.205 pilot mistook it for a P-38, and was then bombed on the ground. In the game it is a generalist with strong guns and ordnance, a decent climb from its air spawn and middling agility. Boom-and-zoom suits it, since a short accurate burst kills most fighters and the guns can tackle high-flying bombers, while its pair of 500 kg bombs can knock out even heavy tanks. Added in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
so_4050_vautour_2a: France's twin-jet S.O.4050 Vautour II was built in separate versions for bombing, close support and all-weather interception; the single-seat IIA, the ground-attack model and the first to appear, was produced from 1956 to 1959 with ATAR 101E3 engines that later variants upgraded to the E5. In the game it is a fast, fairly agile subsonic attacker with enough ordnance for one and a half bases in air battles, though its engines lack WEP. In ground battles it has no ballistic computer and is not nimble enough to bomb moving targets easily, so SNEB rockets plus a light bomb load work better. Added in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
so_4050_vautour_2a_iaf: Israel received 25 ex-French Air Force Vautour IIAs, flying them alongside the IIN on reconnaissance and close support sorties, and used them in the Six-Day and Yom Kippur wars before retiring them soon after. In the game it outperforms most bombers by a wide margin, out-accelerating and outrunning many subsonic jets, and handles respectably for its class. With no means of guiding bombs precisely, it works best skimming the ground and releasing close to the target, which is risky but the most reliable way to knock out bases and ground units. Sold as a premium pack from Update 1.87 "Locked On", it left the store when Update "Winged Lions" arrived.
so_4050_vautour_2a_israel_iaf: France's 1950s Vautour IIA jet attacker served Israel alongside the IIN, carrying cannons, rockets and plenty of ground-attack ordnance for reconnaissance and close support work. In the Israeli tree it flies far better than most bombers, with engines that let it out-accelerate and outpace many subsonic jets, and it manoeuvres reasonably for its size. Lacking any precision bomb-aiming aid, it is most effective in low-level runs that release ordnance right on top of the target: dangerous, but the surest way to destroy bases and ground units. It arrived in Update "Winged Lions".
so_4050_vautour_2b: The Vautour IIB was the dedicated bomber of the French Vautour II family, adding a bomb aimer in a glazed nose ahead of the pilot; 40 were built and some went to Israel in 1960. In the game its task is destroying bases and ground units to drain tickets, and its quick acceleration gets it off the runway ahead of most players. High-altitude bombing works when facing weaker opposition, but with no countermeasures it is exposed to interceptors in uptiers. Rushing a base is usually better, ideally alongside teammates, since it can neither dodge missiles nor out-turn fighters. Added in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
so_4050_vautour_2n: The Vautour IIN was the two-seat all-weather interceptor of the Vautour II programme, armed with four 30 mm DEFA cannons; early aircraft used MACLOS-guided AA-20s instead of Matra R511 radar missiles, and those left unmodified after the 1967–71 upgrades were labelled "Classique". In the game it relies on guns and hard-to-steer AA-20s, which work best unguided in head-on passes, and it faces MiG-19s and F-104s that can easily kill it, so staying low near teammates is wise. Its ground ordnance can still destroy several targets or bases. A premium from Update "Winged Lions" until the 2022 Winter Sale, it returned briefly for Bastille Day in 2023 and 2024.
so_4050_vautour_2n_iaf: Developed from the Vautour IIA with radar and all-weather capability, the two-seat Vautour IIN carried cannons and both infrared and radar-guided missiles; Israeli examples flew until the Mirage IIIC arrived, then passed to the "Knights of the Heart" unit before the A-4E and F-4E replaced them in 1972. Classed as a bomber in the game, it suits air RB and simulator battles, since other modes pit it against modern SPAA and supersonic interceptors. It can destroy nearly two bases in RB, carries four Shafrir missiles for distracted enemies, and its long-range radar is valuable in simulator, especially as few aircraft at its rank have RWR. Added in Update "Winged Lions".
so_4050_vautour_2n_late: The late Vautour IIN was a two-seat all-weather interceptor, nearly supersonic and able to catch Soviet bombers at altitude, using improved ATAR 101E5 engines and a DRAC-32A radar that was strong for its day; it carried AA-20 Nord missiles and later Matra R511s, serving into the 1970s. In the game its engines are powerful but the airframe is sluggish and the weapons mediocre: the R511 radar missile is slow, poorly guided and needs several seconds to reach full manoeuvrability, so even opponents without countermeasures can evade it. Flying above about 3,000 m lets the radar work against climbing enemies such as F-104s. Added in Update "Drone Age".
so_8000_narval: SNCASO's Narval was a late-1940s French naval interceptor prototype driven by a postwar development of the Fw 190D's Jumo 213, supercharged for climb and altitude and meant to fly strike missions too; jet progress ended it in the 1950s. In the game it climbs well, starts with an interceptor spawn, is fast, and carries six MG 151 cannons whose Minengeschoss rounds tear bombers apart in a handful of bursts. Its engine and propeller sit at the back, where pursuers easily disable them, and its poor turn rate makes turning fights a losing proposition. It was a premium pack from Update 1.73 "Vive la France" and later returned for Golden Eagles.
soc_1: Designed by Alexander Solla at Curtiss-Wright, the SOC observation biplane was ordered by the US Navy in 1933, first flew in April 1934 and entered service in November 1935, first aboard the cruiser USS Marblehead; 135 SOC-1s were followed by SOC-2s and SOC-3s until 1938. The OS2U Kingfisher had largely replaced it by 1941, but the failure of the SO3C Seamew brought many back to the front line. In the game it is a shipboard scout for spotting torpedoes and watching enemy movements, with two 7.62 mm Brownings for limited protection and two 100 lb bombs for light targets. Added in Update 2.13 "Winged Lions".
spitfire_f22: One of the final Spitfires, the F Mk 22 developed the Mk 21 with a cut-down rear fuselage and bubble canopy, which caused stability trouble until the Spiteful's rear fuselage and tail were fitted from December 1945. The war's end cut the RAF order from 627 to 260, and some went to Egypt, Rhodesia and Syria. In the game it is among the first "superprops" and plays like the earlier Griffon Spitfires, but with four 20 mm Hispano cannons. Early jets it meets are at a real disadvantage, since it can out-turn most of them and catch them in a dive. It has been in the game since Update 1.39.
spitfire_f24: The F Mk 24 was the final production Spitfire: 54 were made, 27 of them converted from Mk 22s, adding two rear fuselage fuel tanks and mounts for eight RP-3 rockets instead of six. Late examples switched to Hispano Mk V cannons, but the in-game aircraft recreates VN318, which kept the Mk II guns. In the game it is a top-end superprop that flies like the other Griffon Spitfires with four 20 mm cannons, out-turning and diving down most early jets it meets, and 150-octane fuel gives it more engine power than the Mk 22. It was added in Update 1.39.
spitfire_fr_mk14e: This premium FR Mk XIVe wears the scheme of Canadian pilot James Prendergast of No. 414 Squadron RCAF, who flew reconnaissance and strike sorties across Europe ahead of the Normandy landings. The FR XIVe was a low-level reconnaissance Spitfire with a camera, bubble canopy and clipped "e" wing carrying two cannons and two .50 cal guns. In the game the short wings give an excellent roll rate at some cost to turning, and the Griffon 65 out-climbs most opponents, though it trails full-span XIVs at altitude. A premium pack from Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it has since returned in sales and for Golden Eagles at Battle of Britain Day events.
spitfire_fr_mk14e_belgium: After the Second World War the rebuilt Belgian air force chose Spitfires as its general-purpose fighters, and this French-tree FR Mk XIVe carries the markings of Belgian aircraft SG108. The type was a low-altitude reconnaissance variant with a camera, bubble canopy and clipped "e" wing armed with two cannons and two .50 cal machine guns. Its cropped wingtips sharpen the roll rate but cost some turn and pitch performance, while the Griffon 65 lets it out-climb most enemy fighters, although it loses more performance at height than full-span XIVes. It was introduced in Update "Seek & Destroy".
spitfire_ix: From 1943 the low-altitude Merlin 66, with an injection carburettor that cured fuel starvation under negative g, created the LF Mk IX (often called the Mk IXb); it had replaced older-engined IXs by the end of that year, and over 4,000 were built, the most of any Mk IX version. In the game it is a short-ranged interceptor and the highlight of the middle Spitfires: a superb climber that keeps the line's agility, out-turned only by Japanese fighters, while also able to boom-and-zoom. Its weakness is firepower, as the two-cannon, two-machine-gun armament hits lightly beside its rivals. It has been in the game since Update 1.35.
spitfire_ix_early: When the Fw 190 outclassed the Spitfire V in late 1941, the two-stage Merlin 61 was fitted to the Mk Vc airframe as a stopgap, creating the Mk IX: faster, better climbing and more capable at altitude than the Mk V, with belt-fed cannons carrying more ammunition. Merlin 63s took over in 1943 before the LF Mk IX replaced it late that year. In the game it climbs superbly and still turns well, a good bridge to the energy tactics of Griffon Spitfires. Two cannons and four machine guns lack punch against its peers, and its lone 250 lb bomb is useful only against light vehicles and SPAA. Added in Update 1.35.
spitfire_ix_plagis: John Plagis, Southern Rhodesia's top-scoring ace of the war with at least 16 kills, flew this LF Mk IX (ML214, "5J-K") from June to October 1944, claiming four victories and walking away after flak brought him down over Arnhem. In the game it is a short-range interceptor with an outstanding climb rate and classic Spitfire agility, balancing turning and boom-and-zoom well. As a "C" wing aircraft it pairs two Hispano cannons with four .303 Brownings, weaker than the cannon and .50 cal mix on other Spitfires of its period. A premium from Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it left the store in May 2016 and has since returned during several sales and events.
spitfire_ix_usa: The LF Mk IXc refined the Mk IX with a Merlin 66 set up for lower altitude, peaking at around 6 km, plus stronger undercarriage legs, a new intake filter and a broader rudder. From 1942 American units that arrived without aircraft, such as the 52nd Fighter Group, flew British Spitfires, and roughly 1,000 were transferred before Mustangs largely took over in 1944. This example keeps the older armament of two 20 mm Hispano Mk IIs and four 7.7 mm Brownings. It pairs excellent power-to-weight with tight turning and a strong climb, but roll slows at speed, top speed is modest and cannon ammunition is limited. In the game since the open beta.
spitfire_ix_ussr: A Soviet-tree premium Spitfire Mk IXc, this aircraft has been part of the game since the open beta but has only been obtainable for limited periods: for Golden Eagles shortly after Update 1.39 in November 2014, during the 2017 "Spitfire Day" and "Royal Joust" mini-events, as a 2015 "WW2 Chronicles" event reward, and in April of 2022 and 2023 to mark the birthday of Soviet pilot Vasily Macievich.
spitfire_lf_mk9c_cw_greece: Greece, then in the midst of civil war, was given 121 LF and HF Mk IX Spitfires by Britain in January 1947 and used them heavily for armed reconnaissance with rockets, bombs and napalm until 1953; this clipped-wing LF Mk IXc, MH558 "Μύστρας", belonged to Lieutenant Georgios Smyrniotopoulos. Clipping the wings traded lift for a faster roll and more speed down low. In the game it is nearly identical to the tech-tree Spitfire Mk.IX (CW), bar small armament differences: strong at low level and in the climb, but no match for dedicated high-altitude fighters. It was a Battle Pass Season XXIII, "Apollo's Chariot", reward.
spitfire_lf_mk9e_iaf: Clipped wings were fitted to Spitfire Mk IXs to sharpen low-level agility and roll rate, accepting a loss of lift. In the Israeli tree this version handles very well, with acceleration, climb and agility among the best at its rank, though it lacks the ground-attack ordnance carried by fighters such as P-51s and Fw 190s. It is not especially fast, but its climb gets it to altitude sooner than most opponents, and with a height or speed advantage its agility makes it extremely dangerous. It was introduced in Update "Winged Lions".
spitfire_lf_mk9e_weisman: Spitfires formed most of Israel's fighter force by the end of the 1948 war, and this one, once No. 2057, reached Israel in 1949 to fly reconnaissance and escort with 101 Squadron. When most were sold to Burma in 1954, base commander and future president Ezer Weizman argued for keeping a few; repainted black and numbered 57, it became "Weizman's Black Spit", a regular at parades. In the game it climbs and accelerates well and out-turns nearly everything bar some Japanese aircraft, but it has no ground ordnance and a fairly weak engine, so faster, energy-keeping foes punish long fights. A premium pack from Update "Ground Breaking".
spitfire_mk1: Built more than 20,000 times across 24 marks, the Spitfire combined thin elliptical wings with an airframe that could be upgraded into the 1950s; the prototype flew on 5 March 1936, production delays held the first deliveries until mid-1938, and the Mk I made up most of the force in the Battle of Britain. In the game the Mk Ia's 1,030 hp Merlin III gives a strong climb and good speed, but its standout trait is a very tight turn that wins most turning fights, biplanes and Japanese fighters aside. Its eight Browning machine guns fire plenty of rounds yet hit weakly and suffer from convergence. In the game since the open beta.
spitfire_mk14c: Fitting a Griffon 60 into the Mk VIII airframe produced the Spitfire F Mk XIVc, with a fuselage stretched to 9.95 m, extra wing fuel tanks for the thirstier engine, a five-blade Rotol propeller and a "C" wing carrying two 20 mm Hispanos and four 7.7 mm Brownings. Running on 150-octane fuel, it was quick enough to hunt V-1 flying bombs. In the game the Griffon makes it faster than the Merlin Spitfires, though at some cost to agility; it still turns inside most opponents while keeping an excellent climb and good speed. It was introduced in Update 1.41.
spitfire_mk14e: The F Mk XIVe differed from the earlier Griffon-engined Mk XIV in two ways: a cut-down rear fuselage with a bubble canopy for a better view behind, and the "E" wing with two 20 mm Hispanos and two 12.7 mm M2 Brownings in place of the "C" wing's four rifle-calibre guns. In the game the Griffon's extra power makes it faster than Merlin-engined Spitfires, though less nimble; even so, it out-turns most of what it meets and keeps a great climb rate and good speed. It was introduced in Update 1.41.
spitfire_mk18e: Although it resembles the Mk XIV, the Mk XVIIIe was a fresh design rather than a re-engined Mk VIII, with a strengthened airframe and undercarriage to carry extra wing and fuselage fuel. Of 299 built, 99 were fighters and the rest photo-reconnaissance aircraft, all with an "E" wing of two 20 mm Hispanos and two 12.7 mm Brownings; too late for the Second World War, they clashed with Egyptian and Israeli Spitfires over Palestine in 1948–49. In the game its Griffon makes it faster but less agile than Merlin Spitfires, while it still out-turns most rivals and pairs a strong climb with superior firepower. Added in Update 1.41.
spitfire_mk5b: For service in Malta, North Africa, Burma and Australia the Spitfire Mk Vb received a large under-nose air filter, a bigger oil tank, desert survival kit and desert camouflage, accepting the filter's performance penalty. In the game its Merlin 45 gives about 100 hp more than the Mk IIb's Merlin XII once upgraded, improving top speed and high-altitude performance. It keeps the early Spitfires' faults, though: a fragile airframe and wings, poor roll at speed and no combat flaps. It is strongest at close range, and once on an opponent's tail, careful throttle and energy management let it stay there. In the game since the open beta.
spitfire_mk5b_float: Floatplane Spitfires were first considered during the 1940 Norwegian campaign, when airfields were scarce, though the converted Mk I was never flown that way. In 1942 the Mediterranean revived the scheme: three Mk Vbs received floats, enlarged and ventral fins and a four-blade propeller, flew from 12 October 1942 and were trialled on Egypt's Great Bitter Lake, but the islands meant to hide them fell to Germany. In the game it is still nimble and competitive at its rank and can operate from water, though the floats cost performance against the normal Mk Vb and make runways awkward. It was a reward from the 2026 "Wings Over Water" event.
spitfire_mk5b_italy: After the armistice of September 1943 the Allies supplied the Italian Co-Belligerent Air Force with aircraft including Spitfire Mk Vs, which joined 20° Gruppo of 51° Stormo, flying reconnaissance and bomber escort from Lecce-Galatina in 1945 and strafing a German convoy near the Balkans; Mk IXs replaced them in 1946–48. In the Italian tree it plays quite differently from the nation's usual fighters: the 1,440 hp Merlin 45 and light airframe give good speed and climb, and its tight turn is its biggest asset. It fights best at close quarters and, once behind an opponent, careful energy and throttle management keep it there. Added in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
spitfire_mk5b_notrop: The Spitfire Mk V was a stopgap, prompted by high-flying Ju 86 bombers, that put a 1,440 hp Merlin 45 and a negative-g-tolerant carburettor into a Mk I airframe; the Vb, the main production model, carried two Hispano cannons and four .303 Brownings, and the Fw 190 soon outclassed it. In the game it beats the Mk IIb on speed and altitude performance and very slightly edges the tropical Vb, having no air filter. It still has a weak structure, poor high-speed roll and no combat flaps, so it prefers close-range fights and is hard to dislodge once on an enemy's six. Added in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
spitfire_mk5c: The tropical Spitfire Mk Vc gained a large chin air filter, a bigger oil tank and survival equipment for service in Malta, North Africa, Burma and Australia, plus naval camouflage for the Mediterranean and Indian Ocean. In the game it often meets the Bf 109 G-2/trop, stronger in climbs and dives, and the A6M5, which turns better, yet it is far from outmatched. Its Merlin 45M gives excellent acceleration below 3,000 m, it turns well, and four 20 mm Hispano Mk IIs deliver about 5.17 kg/s of burst mass, on a par with the Fw 190 A-5. In the game since the open beta.
spitfire_mk5c_notrop: The Mk Vc was the first Spitfire with the "C" or "Universal" wing, simplified for production and able to take different armament without structural changes, usually four belt-fed 20 mm Hispanos with twice the ammunition of the "B" wing's cannons. Because the Mk IX arrived quickly to counter the Fw 190, the Vc saw little action over Europe, though Mk Vs served widely overseas. In the game it faces the Bf 109 G-2/trop and A6M5 but holds its own, with good turning, strong acceleration below 3,000 m from its Merlin 45M and a heavy 5.17 kg/s burst, performing slightly better than the tropical version. Added in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
spitfire_mk9c_4cannons: The F Mk IX was a stopgap answer to the Fw 190: a two-stage Merlin 61 in a Spitfire Vc airframe, far faster and better at altitude than the Mk V, until the LF Mk IX replaced it in late 1943. This F Mk IXc pairs that engine with the Mk Vc's four 20 mm cannons, so a single good firing chance is often decisive. In the game it climbs exceptionally, has adequate speed and keeps the Spitfire's agility, a good step towards Griffon-style energy fighting. Its single 250 lb bomb suits only light vehicles and SPAA. It was a 2018 "Royal Air Force Centenary" event reward, added in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
spitfire_mk9c_iaf: Facing arms embargoes after independence, Israel bought around 50 Spitfires from Czechoslovakia in 1948 at $23,000 apiece; pilots much preferred them to the Czech-built S-199, and they flew as interceptors and air superiority fighters while P-51s handled longer-range and support missions. Arriving with the first Israeli aircraft tree in Update "Winged Lions", the Mk IXc is a strong dogfighter that out-turns most opponents. Its two 20 mm Hispanos and four 7.7 mm guns have similar muzzle velocities, which makes aiming easier, for example with tracers loaded in the machine guns. Its ground armament also wrecks light vehicles easily and, with careful aim, almost anything else.
spitfire_xvi: The last Merlin-engined Spitfire, the F Mk XVI was an LF Mk IX with the Packard Merlin 266, an American-built Merlin 66; the in-game aircraft has the "E" wing, clipped for better low-level handling at the expense of agility at altitude. With those wings and a bubble canopy it gains an Fw 190-like roll rate, dive, level speed and acceleration over the LF Mk IX. In exchange it turns far worse than other Merlin Spitfires, struggles high up and climbs slightly less well. Two .50 cal Brownings replace the four .303s, a big gain in firepower. In the game since the open beta.
spitfiremkii: The Spitfire Mk II grew out of a 1939 trial that put a 1,175 hp Merlin XII into a Mk I, together with better cooling and an internal starter, and by April 1941 it had replaced every front-line Mk I. The IIb used the "B" wing, swapping the inner .303 guns for 20 mm Hispanos. In the game those cannons fix the IIa's main weakness, but the higher rating shrinks its climb and speed edge over typical opponents, so turning fights against fast German and American fighters matter even more. Cannon ammunition is limited, so short, deliberate bursts pay off. In the game since the open beta.
spitfiremkiia: Born from a 1939 test of a 1,175 hp Merlin XII in a Mk I airframe, the Spitfire Mk II also gained improved cooling and an internal starter, and it had replaced all front-line Mk Is by April 1941. The IIa kept the "A" wing with eight .303 Brownings. In the game it climbs even better than the Mk Ia, helping it seize altitude and set the terms of a fight, and it remains an excellent turn fighter fast enough to run down retreating enemies. The eight machine guns are its weakness: lots of rounds, little hitting power, and convergence issues mean long bursts are needed. Added in Update 1.35.
spitfiremkiia_ep: Presentation Spitfires were paid for through the Spitfire Fund, which let people, firms and towns name an aircraft, and P7923 "Venture I" was one: a Castle Bromwich-built Mk IIa with a Merlin XII and eight Brownings that entered service on 1 February 1941. It flew with 610 Squadron and then 411 Squadron RCAF at Digby, went to the Central Gunnery School in November 1942, struck a parked Miles Master while taxiing in February 1944 and was written off that November. In the game it plays like the tech-tree Mk IIa, climbing well and turning extremely tightly, but its eight machine guns lack punch. Added in Update "Starfighters".
stirling_mk1: Built to Specification B.12/36, the Short Stirling became the first four-engined bomber to join the RAF in wartime, on 7 May 1940, but its bulk left it slower, lower-flying and trickier to take off and land than the Halifax and Lancaster. The B Mk I's four unsupercharged Hercules XI engines faded at altitude, and 708 were made before the Mk III took over in 1943. In the game it is slower and clumsier than the Halifax Mk IIIa; the fragile airframe catches fire easily under cannon hits, and rifle-calibre guns offer little defence. Its 6.4-tonne load of 27 × 500 lb bombs can still destroy several bases. Added in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
stirling_mk3: After complaints about the Mk I's performance, Short fitted the Stirling with supercharged 1,635 hp Hercules XVI engines, creating the B Mk III, which pilots liked when it arrived in 1943. Bomb bay dividers limited it to bombs of 2,000 lb or less, though, and with Halifaxes and Lancasters given priority it left front-line bombing in 1944 for transport and glider towing. In the game it climbs higher and holds speed at altitude much better than the Mk I, but otherwise matches it: poor speed and handling, a big but fragile airframe and weak defensive guns, offset by a heavy bomb load for bases and ground targets. Added in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
strikemaster_mk88: BAC derived the Strikemaster light attacker from the Hunting Jet Provost trainer and first flew it on 26 October 1967; the RAF passed, but 146 were built for export up to 1983. New Zealand's 16 Mk.88s, ordered in 1972 and nicknamed "Blunties" beside No. 14 Squadron's Skyhawks, served until spares shortages forced their replacement in 1991. In the game it is too slow for jet company and meets late-war piston aircraft, but it out-accelerates early jets and keeps energy well. Rockets, bombs and napalm make it a good attacker, while its two 7.62 mm guns are feeble unless gun pods replace the bombs. It was a Battle Pass Season XIII reward.
su-11: When the Su-9's copied Jumo 004 engines disappointed, Sukhoi fitted the domestic Lyulka TR-1s, which demanded new nacelles, wings and a revised tailplane, so the aircraft was renamed Aircraft KM and then Su-11. It flew on 28 May 1947 and could reach 940 km/h at sea level, but instability at speed and a shortage of engines ended the programme in 1948 with one built, and the I-310, the future MiG-15, was chosen instead. In the game it resembles the Su-9 but behaves very differently, with acceleration and top-end speed unmatched at its rank, which makes it a strong premium for researching early Soviet jets. Added in Update "Ixwa Strike".
su-2_m82: The Su-2 (BB-1) light bomber was built from December 1940 to February 1942, 893 in total, and from 1942 mostly spotted for artillery and dropped propaganda leaflets, staying in service until January 1944 through constant repair. In 1941 designers were ordered to fit the new M-82 radial; the resulting version, which restored four forward ShKAS guns and the MV-2 dorsal turret, was tested in February 1942, but only 58 were built. In the game it is a solid ground attacker with bombs and rockets, yet even with more power than the M-88 versions it remains outclassed by enemy fighters. In the game since the open beta.
su-2_mv5: Renamed from BB-1 to Su-2 by decree on 7 December 1940, the Soviet light bomber was refined in production with a cleaner nose, armour behind the MV-5 turret to protect the navigator, and inert-gas protection for the fuel tanks; it later moved to artillery spotting and leaflet drops, serving until January 1944. In the game it suits bomb and rocket attacks on ground targets, and four fast-firing wing ShKAS guns plus a turret gun with wide arcs let it fight back against aircraft. It flies respectably, though fighters still call for caution. The rear armour is its main difference from the BB-1. In the game since the open beta.
su-2_tss1: In 1940 the Su-2's forward armament was cut from four ShKAS to two, and in spring 1941 the heavy MV-5 turret gave way to the lighter TSS-1 to improve performance; the TSS-1 failed its trials with a narrow field of fire and awkward handling, yet 250 aircraft received it before production stopped in May 1941. In the game it remains a capable bomb and rocket carrier, but with only two wing guns and a turret with poorer arcs than other Su-2s it struggles against aircraft. It flies slightly better as a result, though without the MV-5 version's rear armour, so fighters demand caution. In the game since the open beta.
su-6_am42: The final version of Sukhoi's attempt to better the Il-2, the Su-6 (AM-42) kept the M-71F prototype's rear gunner but switched to a Mikulin AM-42 inline, less powerful but more dependable; 1944 trials against the Il-10 favoured Ilyushin, and it never entered production. In the game it is an Il-2-style attacker with better speed and agility but less protection: its rear armour stops little beyond 12.7 mm rounds, and the gunner's 24° traverse limits his usefulness. Air combat beyond head-on passes is best avoided. A broad choice of payloads compensates, including easier-to-aim 23 mm VYa-23s in place of the 37 mm NS-37s. Added in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
su-6_m71: Sukhoi started the Su-6 in 1939 to outdo the Il-2 and flew the first prototype in 1941; engine trouble and wartime evacuation sank the first two, so the third adopted the M-71F radial, a rear gunner with a heavy machine gun prompted by Il-2 combat experience, and two 37 mm wing cannons in place of 23 mm guns. In the game it is a typical attacker: slow and not very agile, but heavily armed. The big cannons are poor for air combat but can kill tanks when well aimed, and two 250 kg bombs plus rockets give it a solid ground-battle loadout, if not for heavy armour. Added in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
su-7b: First of the Su-7s to be mass-produced, the Su-7B appeared once the type was reclassified from fighter to fighter-bomber for the fast, deep strikes against NATO that Soviet doctrine now demanded; the Su-7BM and the widely built Su-7BKL later replaced it. In the game it accelerates very well and outruns nearly every supersonic jet at its rank bar MiG-21s and F-104s, and it handles well enough to tangle with MiG-21s and Harriers without bleeding much energy. It has no guided weapons, but ballistic computers aid bombs and rockets: ZB-360 incendiaries can destroy a whole base, and S-24 or S-5K rockets suit ground battles. Added in Update "Starfighters".
su-7bkl: The Su-7BKL adapted the Su-7B for short and unpaved runways, with rocket boosters that cut the take-off run from 1,250 m to 800 m, an improved brake chute and stronger main gear; about 700 were built up to 1971, more than any other Su-7. In the game it makes a superb fighter-bomber, quick off the mark and often first to the fight, able to flatten a base with four ZB-360s without losing much performance, while its rocket ballistic computer makes S-24s lethal in ground battles. Lacking both missiles and countermeasures, it must stay fast and keep clear of aircraft carrying AIM-9Gs, AIM-9Ls or R-60s. Added in Update "Raining Fire".
su-7bmk: The Su-7BMK was a simplified export model of the Su-7BM sold outside the Warsaw Pact, with Egypt and India among the customers who used it in combat; like the BM it had the stronger, more reliable AL-7F-1 engine and wet pylons for drop tanks. In the game it is probably the strongest Su-7, combining the BM upgrades without the BKL's heavy rough-field equipment, though every Su-7 lacks dogfighting ability, countermeasures and real air-to-air weapons at its rank. Its speed makes it an efficient research tool for quick base bombing. Sold as a premium from Update "Red Skies" until the 2023 May Sale, it briefly returned in January 2024.
su-8: Sukhoi started the Su-8 on 30 June 1941 as a twin-engined heavy attacker for long-range strikes on front-line positions and supply routes, drawing on lessons from the single-engined Su-6. Two prototypes were built, the first flying on 11 March 1943, but the end of M-71 engine development, improved Il-2 versions and fading air force interest ended the project in late 1944. In the game it carries some of the heaviest armament of any attacker and flies surprisingly well, so besides ground attack it can defend itself in the air and threaten enemy aircraft, something the Il-2 cannot. It was a reward from Battle Pass Season VI, "Firepower".
su-9: Sukhoi's "Aircraft K" was one of several Soviet jets rushed forward to match Western designs; it resembled the Me 262 but differed in weight distribution, wing, tail and its flap and airbrake system, and with domestic engines delayed it flew in 1946 on copied Jumo 004s that proved underpowered. Fitting the intended Lyulka TR-1s later produced the Su-11. In the game it is one of the friendliest Soviet starter jets, more forgiving than the MiG-9 and less limited by ammunition and speed than the Yak-15. Its low-velocity mix of two 23 mm and one 37 mm cannon takes practice, but the layout recurs on many later Soviet jets. Added in Update "Ixwa Strike".
su_17m2: Work on upgrading the Su-7 began soon after it entered service in 1959, and after the F-111 showed off variable-geometry wings in 1964, Sukhoi gave its prototype outer wing panels that could pivot; the result flew in 1966 and served widely as the Su-17, exported as the Su-20 and later Su-22, from Vietnam to Peru. In the game the Su-17M2 was the first swing-wing aircraft added and is underwhelming against both opponents and its own tree-mates, but it builds the skills needed for the Su-17M4 and MiG-27s. As the first Soviet supersonic jet with laser-guided weapons, it bridges the Su-25s and Su-7s. Added in Update "Ixwa Strike".
su_17m4: The last Su-17 modernisation, ordered in the late 1970s, added RSDN navigation, the Klyon-57 laser system, an SPO-15LE RWR, TV guidance for the Kh-29T and anti-radiation missile capability; outwardly only extra bleed-air intakes on the rear fuselage set it apart from the M3. It flew in 1980 and left Russian service soon after the USSR broke up. In the game it improves on the Su-17M2 almost everywhere, with a stronger engine and airframe, better ground ordnance, all-aspect R-60Ms and over 250 countermeasures. It is neither the CAS platform the MiG-27 is nor as agile as the MiG-23, but balances both roles well. Added in Update "Danger Zone".
su_22m3: An export Fitter built on the Su-17M3 airframe but powered by a Tumansky R-29BS-300 like that of export MiG-23s, the Su-22M3 went to Syria, where Su-22s fought in 1973 and 1982 and later in the civil war, with losses to MANPADS, Israeli Patriots and a US F/A-18E. In the game it flies much like the Su-17M2 but carries more: up to six R-60s instead of four, and four Kh-25MLs or two Kh-29Ls instead of two Kh-25s or one Kh-29L. It also has countermeasures, which the M2 lacks, although only 12 of them. Added in Update "Winged Lions".
su_22m3_hungary: Hungary bought 12 Su-22M3s and three Su-22UM3 trainers in 1983; after accidents, ten single-seaters and two trainers remained by 1991, flying in reserve until 1997, and some were later sold to Syria, where they gained extra flare dispensers. In the Hungarian sub-tree of the Italian line-up it is identical to the Soviet tree's Su-22M3, with an R-29 engine and Su-17M3 airframe. It carries up to six all-aspect R-60Ms, four Kh-25MLs or two Kh-29Ls and plenty of unguided bombs and rockets, but only 12 countermeasures, rarely enough for more than one threat. Its fast interdiction fills a gap the AMX cannot. Added in Update "Alpha Strike".
su_22m4: East Germany received 48 Su-22M4 fighter-bombers and eight Su-22UM-3K trainers in the 1980s as front-line strike aircraft for a possible war with NATO; after reunification nearly all were scrapped or sold as incompatible with NATO standards, with a few kept in Luftwaffe colours for evaluation. In the German tree it follows the Su-22UM3K and is almost identical to the Soviet Su-17M4.
