It adds TV-guided weapons to laser-guided ones, all-aspect R-60MK missiles and over 250 countermeasures, with an upgraded engine and avionics, making it a strong all-rounder in mixed battles. It arrived in Update "La Royale".
su_22m4_de_wtd61: After reunification the Luftwaffe could not bring East Germany's 48 Su-22M4s, delivered between 1984 and 1987, up to NATO standards, so most were scrapped or sold. Five went to the Bundeswehr's WTD61 test centre, where they flew against NATO fighters to develop tactics and countermeasures before passing to museums. In the game it matches the Soviet Su-17M4 except for its camouflage: slightly slower at altitude than the M3 variants because of its fixed intake, but far better armed, with TV-guided Kh-29Ts, all-aspect R-60MKs and plentiful countermeasures, making it dangerous in air and combined battles. Added in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
su_22um3k: Alongside 48 Su-22M4s, East Germany received eight Su-22UM-3K two-seat trainers in the 1980s; after reunification almost all its Su-22s were scrapped or sold as incompatible with NATO, a few serving the Luftwaffe as test aircraft. In the German tree it is essentially a two-seat Su-22M3 and plays the same fast hit-and-run attacker role, but with 128 countermeasures rather than 12. Laser-guided ground weapons and R-60 missiles for self-defence make it a capable multi-role striker and a stepping stone to the Su-22M4. Added in Update "Wind of Change".
su_24m: The Su-24 "Fencer" began as an all-weather Su-7 derivative but became a new design with side-by-side seats and F-111-style swing wings, entering service in 1975; the Su-24M of 1983 added laser-guided Kh-25 and Kh-29L missiles, KAB-500L and KAB-1500L bombs, R-60Ms and new defensive and navigation systems. In the game this big bomber handles well thanks to two powerful engines and its swing wing, carrying up to 8,000 kg on eight hardpoints, including laser, TV and satellite-guided bombs. Its six-barrel GSh-6-23M and sensitive but capable R-60Ms make it dangerous in the air, though agility is limited and its targeting pod lacks a thermal imager. Added in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
su_25: The Su-25 is a 1970s Soviet close support jet, often likened to the A-10, built in variants including the UB trainer, export K, anti-tank T and SM upgrade, and it has fought in Afghanistan, Chechnya and Georgia. In the game the "Grach" shares the Warthog's long wings, many hardpoints, armoured fuselage and 30 mm cannon, but it is less agile, faster and climbs better, and its precision weapons use laser rather than TV guidance. It struggles against fighters in a fair fight, yet all-aspect R-60Ms and a large stock of heavy countermeasures make it dangerous in the air, while its ordnance devastates ground vehicles. Added in Update "Drone Age".
su_25_558arz: The Su-25BM is a Belarusian upgrade by the 558 Aircraft Repair Plant in Baranovichi for Kazakhstan's air defence forces, which sought the work in 2016; the jets were trialled in mid-2017 and returned to service in 2018 with modern cockpit avionics and new ECM. In the game it has a new HUD and multifunction displays in place of most dials, plus a PS-25 weapons control system that adds R-73 missiles while keeping the full range of air-to-ground stores, from unguided bombs to TV-guided bombs and laser-guided missiles, giving the ageing Frogfoot a new lease of combat value. It was a 2023 Summer Extreme event reward in Update "La Royale".
su_25k: In the early 1970s Soviet close support was judged weak, so a competition for a heavy subsonic attacker was held; Sukhoi's T-8 beat the Il-102 and was ordered in 1978 as the Su-25, reaching Afghanistan the next year, and the Su-25K export model with simpler electronics soon followed. In the game it plays almost exactly like the Su-25. In ground battles its armour, plentiful countermeasures, wide range of guided and unguided ordnance and two R-60MKs make it formidable, and unladen it is stable, surprisingly agile and armed with a strong 30 mm cannon. As a premium it also earns more. Added in Update "Drone Age".
su_25sm3: With the costly Su-25T and TM cancelled, Russia chose the cheaper SM upgrade, aimed mainly at life extension and lower running costs; the SM3 of 2018 was the first true modernisation, adding the Pastel RWR, more dispensers, ECM pods and the SOLT-25 thermal sight. In the game it has fewer air-to-air missiles than the Su-25T and no Vikhrs, but no other Su-25 has thermal optics, and it carries more countermeasures plus a 360° missile warner that can release flares automatically. Its standout weapons are Kh-38ML and MT missiles, the latter reaching ground targets 40 km away, far outside SPAA range. Added in Update "Alpha Strike".
su_25t: Built on the two-seat Su-25UB with the rear cockpit replaced by fuel and electronics, the Su-25T tank hunter gained a new fire control system, racks for up to eight Vikhrs per pylon, the Ka-50's Shkval sight, a depressible 30 mm cannon, tail-mounted countermeasures and an IRCM unit. A few did well in Chechnya in 1994, but cost ended the programme in 2000 after only eleven were built. In the game it is formidable in mixed battles, with TV and laser-guided weapons, Vikhrs, strong optics, plentiful flares and IRCM. In air battles fourth-generation fighters and IRCCM missiles blunt those tools, leaving awareness, the IRCM and R-73s to keep it alive. Added in Update "La Royale".
su_25tm: The Su-25TM, marketed for export as the Su-39, appeared in the late 1990s as a further development of the Su-25 shaped by experience in Afghanistan and Chechnya, with improved avionics and targeting systems and precision weapons for use against land and sea targets. In the game it is a dedicated precision striker built around three guided missile types: long-reaching, accurate Kh-29s for fortified or high-value targets, Kh-25s for quick reaction against urgent threats, and Vikhrs for picking off armour. It was added in Update "La Royale".
su_27: After Soviet intelligence learned of the US F-X programme in 1969, the USSR adopted a similar mix of heavy and light fighters, giving Sukhoi the heavy one; the troubled T-10 was reworked with TsAGI, the Su-27 flew in 1977, and production aircraft entered service in 1985. In the game the Flanker is a generalist: ten missiles, including up to six HMD-cued infrared ones and four R-27ERs guided by the N001 radar, let it strike from range, and its unstable fly-by-wire airframe allows high-AoA and post-stall moves such as the Cobra. Its big heat signature makes IRCCM missiles a threat, and better-powered F-15s can beat it in some fights. Added in Update "Air Superiority".
su_27sm: When post-Soviet budgets killed new projects such as the Su-37 and MiG-1.44, Russia upgraded existing jets instead, starting with the Su-27SM: a modern cockpit with HOTAS and multifunction displays, GLONASS navigation, an improved radar and IRST compatible with R-77 and Kh-29 weapons, the Pastel RWR and Khibiny jamming pods. It entered service in the early 2000s. In the game it is very similar to the Su-27 but adds R-77 active radar missiles and guided ground weapons, including KAB-500 bombs, Kh-29TD missiles and the huge KAB-1500Kr. It keeps the original's few countermeasures, mediocre radar and unstable handling. Added in Update "Seek & Destroy".
su_30mk2v_venezuela: The Su-30MK2 grew from the Su-30MKK built at KnAAPO for China, adding anti-ship weapons and the N001VEP radar in 2002. Venezuela ordered 24 in 2006, first designated Su-30MK2V and renamed Su-30MK2 AMV after Vietnam also bought the type; all arrived within three years and are still flying, minus three lost in accidents. In the Soviet tree it is heavy, with low thrust-to-weight, so drawn-out close-range manoeuvring is a poor idea. Capable medium- and short-range missiles make up for this, and varied air-to-ground weapons let it hit both fixed and moving targets. Added in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
su_30mkk: After the Gulf War, China's military sought precision long-range strike capability and, having received Su-27SKs in 1992, negotiated for a more attack-capable aircraft; a 1999 contract for 38 Su-30MKKs followed, with a reinforced airframe and gear, composite fins, new avionics and the N001VE radar, and a second batch of 38 was ordered in 2001. Today the PLAAF operates 73. In the game it is essentially the Venezuelan Su-30MK2 AMV with Chinese air-to-air missiles: heavy and underpowered for close dogfights, but its large payload suits medium and long-range combat, and its air-to-ground weapons cover fixed and moving targets. Added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
su_30mkm: Malaysia ordered 18 Su-30MKMs, derived from India's Su-30MKI, in a 2003 deal worth US$900 million; India built the wings and tail surfaces, deliveries ran from 2007 to 2009, and in 2016 it became the first Russian-built jet to drop a GBU-12 Paveway. Engine problems grounded 14 by 2018 until a local refit finished in 2025. In the Japanese tree it is almost the same as the Soviet Su-30SM, with thrust vectoring for low-speed agility and long-ranged RVV-SD missiles, but adds a DAMOCLES thermal pod and missile and laser warning. Its weight and modest engine thrust hurt acceleration and manoeuvring. Added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
su_30sm: The Su-30 began in 1986 as the Su-27PU, a two-seat long-range interceptor and command aircraft for the air defence forces, which found the early Su-27 short on range; it first flew at Irkutsk at the end of 1989. India's canard-equipped, thrust-vectoring Su-30MKI spawned many export versions and, in the mid-2010s, the Su-30SM for Russia's own air force. In the game it combines weapons from across the Flanker family, including the Su-34, with modern avionics and sensors, while canards and thrust vectoring make it highly agile. It is a genuine top-tier Soviet fighter, able to compete with the F-15E, Typhoon and Rafale. Added in Update "Hornet's Sting".
su_30sm2: Unveiled in 2020 and delivered from 2021–22, notably to naval aviation, the Su-30SM2 brings Su-35S technology to the two-seat Su-30, chiefly the long-range Irbis radar, which can track several targets at once, and stronger, more economical AL-41F-1S engines with all-aspect thrust vectoring; it is steadily taking over from the Su-30SM. In the game it keeps the SM's strengths: thrust-vectored agility, good speed, many missiles and a wide range of guided weapons. The new radar's broad coverage is the main gain, while size and weight make it lose speed and energy more quickly than lighter Western jets. Added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
su_33: Work on a carrier Flanker for the Admiral Kuznetsov began in 1984 as the Su-27K, which flew on 17 August 1987 with stronger gear, folding wings and tailplanes, a hook and canards for slow approaches; it entered Russian Navy service as the Su-33 in 1998. In the game it keeps much of the Su-27's performance and can take as many as 12 air-to-air missiles, mixing R-73s, R-27ERs and long-range infrared R-27ETs. It has no thrust vectoring and is less agile than an F-16 or Gripen, but it is steady at low speed, and its radar, IRST and HMD suit multirole work. Only 48 countermeasures is its main weakness. Added in Update "Storm Warning".
su_34: Sukhoi began planning a Su-27-based replacement for the Su-24 in the 1980s, using the two-seat Su-27UB as a starting point so a weapons officer could join the pilot; the first prototype flew in 1990, but pre-production was delayed until 2005 and the first large order came in 2008. In the game it blends the strike strengths of the Su-25 and Su-24, with a heavy payload and one of the broadest precision arsenals available, including satellite-guided bombs, many air-to-ground missiles and the Grom-2 glide bomb. Plenty of air-to-air missiles let it fight too, but it is heavy and lacks the speed and agility of comparable jets. Added in Update "Firebirds".
su_6_single: Sukhoi began the single-seat Su-6 attacker in 1939, and it outperformed the Il-2, but its radial engine reached the end of its permitted life before testing finished and no replacements existed; later prototypes added a rear gunner, yet the Il-10 kept the type from production. This is the first prototype, without a gunner and with the weaker M-71. In the game it is competitive: top speed, acceleration and climb are mediocre, but it turns well, and twin 23 mm cannons make short work of soft ground targets and most aircraft with the right belts. Its bombs and rockets are small, so they need accurate delivery. Added in Update "Raining Fire".
sunderland_mk3a: Short's S.25 Sunderland was derived from the Empire flying boat airliner to meet Specification R.2/33; it first flew on 16 October 1937, a prototype set a record on a flight to Singapore in 1938, and it became the RAF's main wartime anti-submarine patrol aircraft. The Mk III was the most numerous version, with a revised hull for better seaworthiness and room for more defensive guns. In the game it is a classic flying boat, big and slow but well defended, and its hull absorbs plenty of hits from the small-calibre guns most opponents carry. Its four forward-firing nose guns are of little use against aircraft given its speed and agility. Added in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
sunderland_mk5: Crews felt the Sunderland's Bristol Pegasus engines lacked power, so the late-war Mk V switched to Pratt & Whitney Twin Wasps, already common in RAF service on Catalinas and Dakotas, which eased supply and maintenance; 155 were built and 33 Mk IIIs converted. In the game it is still a big, slow flying boat, but the new engines raise top speed and climb, and two .50 cal waist guns strengthen its defences. At its rank, however, heavier-armed fighters and SPAA start to appear and the once very tough airframe no longer holds up, so keeping engagements at long range is wise. Added in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
super_etendard_97: When the naval Jaguar was cancelled, France modernised its carrier-borne Etendard IVM rather than import A-4s or A-7s, giving the Super Etendard a new engine and Dassault avionics proven on late Mirage IIIs and early Mirage 2000s, which brought anti-ship and laser-guided weapons. In the game it is competitive in both roles: it can go supersonic without afterburner at some altitudes, and plentiful countermeasures plus R.550 Magic 1 missiles help in dogfights. It shines in mixed battles, with up to four GBU-12s, an ATLIS II pod and an air-to-ground radar that can spot vehicles from afar. Added in Update "Sons of Attila".
super_hind_mk3: The Superhind is a South African Mi-24 modernisation by ATE, which turned to the type in 1996 after its Rooivalk work and offered Mk.II to Mk.V packages with modern weapons, navigation and all-weather capability; Algeria upgraded 40 Mi-24Vs from 1999, but marketing to new NATO members in Eastern Europe produced only a demonstrator for Bulgaria. In the game its nose-mounted 20 mm cannon with an advanced thermal sight is excellent against lightly armoured vehicles, and it can carry unguided bombs and rockets plus tandem-warhead INGWE missiles reaching 5 km. With no air-to-air missiles, it is poorly suited to fighting aircraft. Added in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
sw_a_34_comet: This Comet I is one of the tanks Finland imported in 1958 as trainers for the Charioteers bought alongside them, and in the Swedish tree it performs identically to the British original. Its 77 mm HV gun, effectively a lower-velocity 17-pounder, is among the stronger guns on a medium of its rating, especially once APDS is unlocked. Mobility is excellent, with quick acceleration to its 38 km/h top speed, though reverse is painfully slow, and gun depression is far better than on the Sherman Firefly, helping it fight hull-down. Its armour is easily penetrated, so its low profile and speed are its real protection. Added in Update "Fire and Ice".
sw_asrad_r: Developed by Rheinmetall and Saab Bofors Dynamics, ASRAD-R is a short-range air defence system, here on an M113, that works with either a 3D AESA radar reaching 20 km or an IRST and fires laser-beam-riding RBS-70 (Bolide) missiles, able to intercept even cruise missiles, from an unmanned launcher raised well above the hull. In the game it improves on the Lvrbv 701: the high launcher lets the hull stay in cover while covering all directions, and eight long-range supersonic missiles make it deadly, especially to helicopters. Their HEAT warheads can also knock out light tanks, APCs and IFVs, though not MBTs. Added in Update "Hot Tracks".
sw_bkan_1c: Bofors developed the bandkanon 1 in 1960–65 as an autoloading 155 mm self-propelled gun on S-tank running gear; 26 were delivered with the Strv 103A's weak powerplant, and a 1988 upgrade fitted the Strv 103C's piston engine, creating the Bkan 1C, which served until 2003. In the game its huge gun fires powerful HE and HE-VT shells with a reload of just 3.2 seconds, but it is very sluggish, thinly armoured, carries only 14 rounds and has just -2° of depression and limited traverse. Light and medium targets fall easily, while heavy ones like the Ferdinand or Maus need hits on the roof or cupola. Added in Update "Winged Lions".
sw_bmp_2md: By 2016 the BMP-2s Finland bought in 1988 were outdated, so 100 were upgraded to BMP-2MD standard with storage boxes doubling as spaced armour, thermal signature reduction, modern thermal optics for gunner, driver and commander, and new radios, raising weight from 13.1 to 13.5 tonnes. In the Swedish tree it gives up the Soviet BMP-2's ATGMs in exchange for modern thermal sights and a little more armour. Otherwise it is the same BMP: thinly protected, able to threaten tanks only through their weaker side armour, and at times less mobile than main battle tanks. Added in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
sw_bt_42: Finland captured BT-7 light tanks during the Winter and Continuation Wars, and because their 37/45 mm guns were too weak, 18 were rebuilt with a new turret carrying a British 4.5-inch howitzer as the BT-42 assault gun; only one survived the war and later scrapping. In the game it is one of the best-known Finnish light tanks and something of a meme thanks to an appearance in a Japanese animated film, pairing the hard-hitting QF 4.5-inch howitzer with the speed and agility typical of BT tanks. Added in Update "Fire and Ice".
sw_charioteer_mk_7: Finland's tank force of the 1950s relied on obsolete T-26s and ageing T-34s, Panzer IVs and StuG IIIs short of spares, so three used Charioteer Mk VIIs were bought for trials in late 1957; they did well, and Britain sold 35 more after overhaul in 1960, with all 38 serving actively until the late 1970s. In the Swedish tree its armour is weak, but the 20-pounder gun can destroy almost any opponent from the front, and decent mobility lets it reach good positions quickly to hold back enemy advances. Added in Update 2.21 "Fire and Ice".
sw_crotale_ng: ItO 90 is Finland's name for the Crotale NG short-range missile system on the Patria Pasi XA-181 6x6. Thomson-CSF and Rockwell created the original Crotale in the 1960s, and its NG modernisation brought the VT-1 missile and new radar; Finland received 20 vehicles by 1993 and upgraded them to ItO 90M standard with a thermal imager in 2007. In the game the fast, highly manoeuvrable VT-1 can engage aircraft out to about 12 km, and the thermal sight helps at night and in poor weather. Being so large, it struggles to find cover from aircraft or tanks. Added in Update 2.7 "Red Skies".
sw_cv_90105: Built from the start to accept different turrets, the CV 90 was paired in 1993 with GIAT's TML 105 turret, which brought thermal sights, modern fire control and Galix smoke dischargers; the resulting light tank was shown at Eurosatory in June 1994 but drew no interest. In the game it shares little with the later CV 90105 beyond the name, lacking both autoloader and stabiliser. It is still quick, with thermals, a laser rangefinder and reasonable ammunition, but its armour is as thin as on every other CV 90. Added in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
sw_cv_90105_tml: Revealed in 2014, the CV90105 was a joint CMI Defence and BAE Systems Hägglunds project mating the Cockerill XC-8 turret, with a stabilised, autoloaded 105 mm gun, to the combat-proven CV90 chassis. It first appeared in the game in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury" under the TML name with a Nexter turret, then was almost entirely remodelled in Update "Drone Age". Its 105 mm gun is modest where most MBTs carry 120 mm, but excellent fire control, second-generation thermals and a stabilised commander's sight compensate. Frontal armour shrugs off HEAT and even 57 mm autocannon fire, and good mobility and reverse speed make relocating easy.
sw_cv_90120: After the CV 90105, its makers developed a successor on the same chassis with a Swiss Ordnance Enterprise 120 mm gun for MBT-level firepower, keeping weight down so speed and fire control would remain its protection; the CV90120-T was shown in its final form in 2011. In the game it adds a stronger gun and a very fast autoloader to the CV 90105 formula, but its armour barely stops heavy machine-gun AP from the front, and 12.7 mm rounds can pierce the sides. In return its fire control is among the game's finest, with third-generation optics and a commander's sight zooming to 24x. Added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
sw_cv_9030_fin: The CV 9030 is an export CV90 Mk.II with Hägglunds' E-series turret and a 30 mm Bushmaster, built for Finland, Switzerland and Norway; Finnish vehicles, designated CV 9030 FIN, use a Soviet PKT coaxial gun, and 102 were bought in 1998 and 2004, all still in service. In the game its belt-fed 30 mm Bushmaster fires more slowly than the 40 mm Akan m/70Bc on other CV90s, and the commander gets his own thermal sight. Beyond that it is a typical CV90: mobile but poorly protected. Added in Update 2.27 "La Royale".
sw_cv_9035_dk: Denmark's M113s were badly outgunned by the 1990s, as service in Bosnia showed, so 2003 trials picked the Swedish Strf 90, and Denmark then took an updated CV9035 Mk.III with a 35 mm cannon, ordering 45 in December 2005 with Swedish hulls, Danish-built turrets, modern electronics and a stronger engine. They entered service from June 2008, and ten deployed briefly to Afghanistan in 2010. In the game its 35 mm Bushmaster III, a larger version of the CV9030FIN's gun, sets it apart from other CV90s, and it has thermal sights and moves well, but armour is weak and there are no ATGMs. Added in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
sw_cv_90_mk4: Work on a new CV 90 generation started in 2016, drawing on the Mk II and Mk III, and the Mk.IV was unveiled in January 2018; a 1,000 hp Scania DS16 and upgraded Perkins X300 transmission keep it nimble at up to 38 tonnes, and it is now reaching customers such as the Czech Republic. In the game its fast-firing 30 mm Bushmaster II Mk. 44 deals with most targets, Spike-LR missiles destroy armour at long range, and mobility is excellent. Protection is only mediocre, though, so well-armoured opponents call for caution. Added in Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
sw_eldenhet_98: Sweden took part in the IRIS-T missile programme, and the Eldenhet 98 uses IRIS-T SL missiles to replace the ageing RBS 70: on an articulated BvS 10 all-terrain vehicle, the leading unit holds a command module with radar and the trailing one the launcher. The prototype was first shown in August 2016 at Malmen during the Swedish Air Force's 90th anniversary, and the number in service is not known. In the game the radar unit and trailer-mounted launcher work together, and the infrared-guided IRIS-T SL hits aircraft accurately at long range. It is poorly protected and has no way to fight ground vehicles. Added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
sw_ikv_103: The Ikv 103 traces back to a 1949 requirement for a small, light, cheap assault gun, first met by the Ikv 72 and upgraded to Ikv 102 standard in 1956. The 103 swapped the 75 mm gun for a 105 mm, added an armoured roof and a Volvo B42 engine, and moved the air intake to rear grilles. In the game it is tiny and thinly armoured but hits hard, its 105 mm HEAT-FS round, unusual at its rank, able to handle tanks like the T95. Mobility is mediocre despite neutral steering, it has no machine gun to clear fences that set off HEAT, and even 12.7 mm fire can penetrate it. Added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
sw_ikv_72: The early Cold War Swedish Army wanted a small, mobile self-propelled gun, cheap enough to build in numbers, to replace towed artillery in support of infantry; the first such Infanterikanonvagn was the 75 mm Ikv 72, of which 36 were built, serving until the Ikv 102 began replacing it in the late 1950s. In the game it is a capable light tank destroyer whose mobility suits flanking slower enemy tanks. Its low-velocity 580 m/s shells and middling penetration make sniping harder than in most tank destroyers, and with no armour or roof it is easy prey for artillery, aircraft, autocannons and heavy machine guns. Added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
sw_ikv_73: The Ikv 73 descends from the Lago I, a 1930s export design for Hungary that became Sweden's Strv m/42; when the Strv m/42 EH was retired after the Strv 81 arrived in the 1950s, it was reworked into an infantry support tank, largely unchanged apart from a turret modified for a roof-mounted machine gun. In the game it plays like the m/42 EH, but the roof MG replaces the hull gun, helping against aircraft and open-topped vehicles. It is faster than most mediums, though slow in reverse. Penetration is poor against KV-1s and T-34s, but when its APHE gets through, the large filler often knocks out the crew. A 2020 Operation S.U.M.M.E.R. reward.
sw_ikv_91: Hägglund & Söner built around 212 Ikv 91 infantry support vehicles from 1975 to 1978; the low-pressure 90 mm gun and laser rangefinder handled light vehicles and infantry, but by the 1980s it could not beat newer Soviet tanks, and a 105 mm upgrade was judged too costly for the light hull and turret. It left service in 2002, replaced by the CV90. In the game it was Sweden's first modern infantry support tank, and its laser rangefinder and excellent optics make it a precise long-range shooter despite low muzzle velocity. Thin armour leaves it vulnerable even to heavy machine guns up close, so it works best behind heavier tanks. Added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
sw_ikv_91_105: After the Ikv 91 impressed India in 1982 trials against the AMX-10 PAC 90 but was judged under-gunned, Hägglunds developed the Ikv 91-105 with Rheinmetall's low-recoil Rh 105-20 gun, generating 200 kN of recoil against the L7's 600 kN, plus new fire control and infrared night sights. India never adopted it, and Sweden, doubting the chassis, chose other vehicles. In the game it lacks thermals but is very mobile, making it dangerous on flanks, and its slpprj m/80 round, two-axis stabiliser and laser rangefinder let it fire first. Gun depression is adequate, but reverse is slow, so smoke helps when backing away. Added in Update "Ixwa Strike".
sw_itpsv_90: Finland bought seven British Marksman anti-aircraft turrets in 1990 and fitted them to Polish-built T-55AM hulls; as those aged, the systems were stored from 2010 and moved to seven surplus Leopard 2A4 chassis, entering service as the ItPsV 90 in 2015. In the game this Leopard-based Marksman gains greatly in mobility from the powerful MTU diesel, letting it reposition wherever air cover is needed. It gives Swedish players dependable air defence and can handle both aircraft and ground vehicles with relative ease. Added in Update "Sky Guardians".
sw_k9_vidar: VIDAR is Norway's variant of the South Korean K9 Thunder, in service since 2019 with Brigade Nord's artillery battalion after orders for 24 in 2017 and four more in 2022; it adds the domestic ODIN fire control system and direct-fire equipment. In the game it is one of few vehicles at its rank with both a thermal imager and a laser rangefinder, and its 155 mm HE can destroy most tanks, though heavy ones need precise hits. Turret traverse is slow, there is no stabiliser, armour is thin and depression limited, but it moves well for its size and reverses at 42 km/h. Added in Update "Sons of Attila".
sw_kungstiger: In 1946 France let a Swedish delegation pick three surplus German vehicles free of charge for trials, and Sweden asked for the best King Tiger available; after a burnt-out wreck in Normandy was rejected, a well-preserved example found south of Paris reached Stockholm in late 1947 and went to P 4 at Skövde for evaluation. In the game it plays like the German Tiger II (P): its 88 mm KwK43 penetrates well at range, struggling only with the toughest heavies such as the Maus and IS-4M. The hull armour is excellent, but the early turret's cheeks are a weak spot, so long-range fighting suits it best. A Battle Pass Season XV reward.
sw_kv_1_1942_fin: Finland had no tank industry of its own, so it repaired abandoned Soviet armour and put it into service, including at least two captured KV-1 heavy tanks, a KV-1E and a Model 1942. Their thick armour made them useful for breaking through Soviet lines and in the late-war defensive battles, and both survived and are now displayed at the Parola tank museum. In the Swedish tree it is heavily armoured, reasonably mobile and penetrates well, but it turns poorly, reverses slowly and its turret weak spots are well known to experienced players. Added in Update 2.39 "Dance of the Dragons".
sw_l_62_anti_II: Landsverk's L-62 ANTI II improved on the Anti I with a better hull and turret mounting a 40 mm Bofors L/60 on the interwar L-60 light tank chassis. Finland bought six in 1942, which were credited with 11 Soviet aircraft in the Continuation War and served until 1966. In the game its 40 mm HE can down most aircraft with one hit, while APC and SAPHEI rounds handle most tanks at its rank if aimed at weak spots. It feels sluggish, has only -5° of depression and a slow 120 rpm rate of fire, and its open top leaves the crew exposed to HE and HEAT. Added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
sw_lago_1: Designed in Sweden for export to Hungary, the Lago I medium tank lost its customer when Hungary chose to develop its own design with Škoda's help; the Swedish Army later trialled it and developed it into the long-serving Strv m/42. In the game it plays rather like an early Panzer III: quick and agile, without much firepower, although post-war APDS rounds give it strong penetration at range, where its angled armour protects it well. A compact breech allows excellent gun depression for firing over crests without much exposure. Added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
sw_landsverk_ush_204_gk: Daimler-Benz and Landsverk teamed up in 1956 to armour the Unimog S military truck, producing the rear-engined Unimog-SH, which sold in small numbers to India, Belgium and Ireland. A 1960s derivative armed with a 20 mm Oerlikon 204GK (KAA-01) cannon, the U-SH 204 GK, attracted no orders, and what became of the single prototype is unknown. In the game it is small and fast, with a very effective 20 mm gun against aircraft, much like the Italian R3 T20 FA-HS. It shares the R3's weak armour too, and its gun cannot penetrate heavily armoured tanks, even from the side or rear. Added in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
sw_landsverk_ush_405: Landsverk and Daimler-Benz built this late-1950s prototype on a Unimog 404 truck chassis, fitting it with twin 81 mm Oerlikon rocket launchers; it was the only one made, and without orders the idea was dropped. In the game its speed, agility and excellent reverse suit ambushes and quick strikes: the drum-fed launchers fire rapidly, swamping a target with rockets before the vehicle slips away. The brakes are nearly useless, though, making it hard to slow down, and since it is really an armoured car, autocannons and even heavy machine guns can destroy it. Added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
